texts.value: Catalyzes the reduction of uracil and thymine in the initial step of reductive pyrimidine catabolism, a pathway that yields beta-alanine from uracil and beta-aminoisobutyrate from thymine (PubMed:1512248). Also capable of degrading the chemotherapeutic drug 5-fluorouracil (PubMed:1512248)
Binds 4 [4Fe-4S] clusters per subunit. Contains approximately 16 iron atoms per subunit.
Found in most tissues with greatest activity found in liver and peripheral blood mononuclear cells

disease.description: A metabolic disorder with large phenotypic variability, ranging from no symptoms to a convulsive disorder with motor and intellectual disability. It is characterized by persistent urinary excretion of excessive amounts of uracil, thymine and 5-hydroxymethyluracil. Patients suffering from this disease show a severe reaction to the anticancer drug 5-fluorouracil.

texts.value: The disease is caused by variants affecting the gene represented in this entry
Belongs to the dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase family
